title: Hybrid INT8/FP8 profile verification using probabilistic slice simulation for reranker quality
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a robust verification harness and playbook to validate hybrid INT8/FP8 quantization profiles for the reranker model family. This ticket scopes building a probabilistic slice-simulation framework that (a) synthesizes realistic candidate-distribution shifts per customer slice, (b) runs calibration sweeps across per-layer and per-channel scale choices, and (c) computes statistically reliable NDCG@10 and MRR deltas with confidence intervals and slice-aware reporting. The goal is to catch rare regression modes that small-sample aggregate tests miss and to produce a deterministic rollout checklist (canary → ramp → full rollout) for profile promotion to production.

Background and motivation:
- Prior calibrations found small global NDCG regressions that masked significant per-slice degradations.
- Hybrid quantization (FP8 for attention/FFN critical tensors + INT8 for embedding and output projections) shows promising cost/latency reductions but increases variance across query slices.
- We need an automated method to simulate realistic slice-level shifts (query length, candidate set size, score distribution skew) so we can estimate worst-case slice regressions and required rollback triggers.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Implement probabilistic slice simulator that can sample from existing telemetry-driven priors and generate synthetic candidate sets preserving token-length and score covariance statistics.
2) Hook the simulator into the existing quant-calib pipeline to run: per-layer scale sweep, asymmetric vs symmetric calibration, and mixed-precision masks.
3) Compute NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals; report both global and per-slice metrics.
4) Define hard acceptance thresholds and automated gating rules for staging promotion (see acceptance_criteria).
5) Produce a reproducible experiment artifact (notebook + saved seeds + config) and link a PR that adds this workflow to CI/regression harness.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Implementing hardware kernel changes.
- Large-scale production rollouts (only providing checklist and metrics).

Notes on methodology:
- Use telemetry histograms (query length, candidate_count, original score distribution skew, top-1 entropy) as priors for the generator.
- For each simulated slice, draw 5000 candidate-query pairs by default and run both fp64 baseline and hybrid quantized variants; if a real-slice mapping exists, run smaller targeted experiments on the real example set.
- Apply block-bootstrap per-query to build confidence intervals for NDCG/MRR deltas. Report the fraction of bootstraps where quantized < baseline by threshold to estimate p(regression).
- Compute Kullback-Leibler divergence between baseline and quantized score distributions to surface score-shift modes; flag slices where KL>0.05 for detailed inspection.
- Track latency and memory metrics for each profile to quantify tradeoffs.

Deliverables:
- code: simulator + pipeline integration (python, pytest coverage)
- analysis notebook with sample runs and visualizations (per-slice waterfall charts, KL heatmaps, bootstrap delta histograms)
- deterministic experiment bundle (seed, config.json, sample slice manifests)
- rollout checklist and gating rules to be stored in Console docs

Technical risks and mitigations:
- Risk: simulator priors poorly model real-world rare slices. Mitigation: bootstrap priors from telemetry and include a "record-and-replay" export for customers where we have labeled slices.
- Risk: long runtime for bootstrapping. Mitigation: stratified sampling and early-stopping when bootstrap CI stabilizes; run heavy experiments on dedicated infra.
- Risk: noise from non-deterministic GPU kernels. Mitigation: pin seeds, use deterministic kernels where possible, run multiple repeats and average.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can produce per-slice NDCG@10 and MRR deltas with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals
Global NDCG@10 drop must be < 0.5% (median) AND per-slice drop must be < 2.0% for all monitored slices, otherwise profile is rejected
MRR drop < 1.0% (median) and per-slice MRR drop < 3.0% for monitored slices
Produce artifact with deterministic seed, config, and a launchable notebook demonstrating at least three simulated slices (short queries, long queries, and skewed score distributions)
Generate gating report (JSON) that can be consumed by the staging CI to allow/deny profile promotion
Add unit tests / integration tests covering simulator sampling and bootstrap CI computations
steps: Collect telemetry priors and create slice manifests (owner: Marco) — 1 day
Prototype probabilistic slice simulator and validate against held-out real slices — 3 days
Integrate simulator with existing quant calibration pipeline; add per-layer sweep configs — 2 days
Implement bootstrap CI and KL divergence reporting, add visualization notebook — 2 days
Run end-to-end experiments for 5 candidate profiles, produce gating reports — 2 days
Write rollout checklist and add CI gating hook, create PR and request review — 1 day
notes: When running on dedicated infra, use the 'quant-staging' GPU pool with determinism flags enabled. If a candidate profile passes the simulator but fails on a small real-slice test, mark it as 'requires additional calibration' and follow the remediation steps in the playbook.
postmortem_actions: If any slice fails gating in production canary, capture top-k queries and run 'record-and-replay' with expanded candidate sets
Log failure modes to the ranking-quantization-incident board and attach the gating JSON
